data.title: Folliculitis — viva
data.summary: Bacterial infections · 10 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Folliculitis** (Bacterial infections)_

**Q1. Define folliculitis.**
- Inflammation of the hair follicle (histologically inflammatory cells in the wall and ostium) producing a follicular papule or pustule; superficial (infundibulum) or deep (whole follicle)

**Q2. Classify folliculitis.**
- Infective: bacterial (S. aureus — superficial/Bockhart, sycosis barbae; Gram-negative folliculitis in acne on long-term antibiotics; Pseudomonas hot-tub folliculitis), fungal (Malassezia, dermatophyte — Majocchi), viral (herpetic, molluscum), parasitic (Demodex)
- Non-infective: eosinophilic pustular folliculitis (Ofuji, HIV-associated), perforating folliculitis, acne keloidalis nuchae, pseudofolliculitis barbae, folliculitis decalvans, drug-induced (steroids, EGFR inhibitors), occupational (oil/tar)

**Q3. What is sycosis barbae and how is it different from tinea barbae and pseudofolliculitis barbae?**
- Sycosis barbae: deep staphylococcal folliculitis of the beard, chronic, upper lip involved
- Tinea barbae: zoophilic dermatophyte, kerion-like boggy plaques, hairs easily pluckable, usually spares upper lip
- Pseudofolliculitis barbae: ingrown curly hairs after close shaving; not infective

**Q4. What is hot-tub folliculitis?**
- Pseudomonas aeruginosa folliculitis 8–48 h after contaminated hot tub/swimming pool; pruritic follicular papulopustules on trunk under swimwear; self-limiting; ciprofloxacin if severe

**Q5. What is Gram-negative folliculitis?**
- Pustules around nose/chin in acne patients on long-term tetracyclines (Klebsiella, Enterobacter, Proteus); treat with isotretinoin

**Q6. What is follicular triad and tetrad?**
- Triad: acne conglobata, hidradenitis suppurativa, dissecting cellulitis of scalp
- Tetrad: triad + pilonidal sinus

**Q7. Investigations?**
- Gram stain and culture of pustule; KOH for fungal; Demodex mount; biopsy for non-infective types; check for nasal carriage, diabetes in recurrent cases

**Q8. Treatment?**
- Antiseptic washes (chlorhexidine/BPO), topical mupirocin/fusidic acid; oral cloxacillin/cephalexin for extensive; treat carriage
- Avoid occlusion, shaving with clean blade or stop shaving; specific therapy for non-bacterial types (e.g. indomethacin for eosinophilic pustular folliculitis, antifungal for Malassezia)

**Q9. What is infundibular folliculitis?**
- Disseminate and recurrent infundibulofolliculitis — skin-coloured follicular papules on trunk in dark-skinned young men; non-infective; treated with isotretinoin, emollients, keratolytics

**Q10. What is LMDF?**
- Lupus miliaris disseminatus faciei — reddish-brown papules on central face incl. eyelids; caseating granulomas; now considered granulomatous rosacea variant/separate entity; heals with pitted scars; doxycycline, isotretinoin, dapsone

## Quick spotter facts
- Follicular pustules with central hair — folliculitis; tender nodule — furuncle

_Sources: DYP Survival Guide for PG Dermatology Exam (Bacterial infections — folliculitis, infundibular folliculitis, LMDF); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e ch.15. Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
